fact: Many decisions arise via the accumulation of noisy evidence to a threshold or bound.
source_span: Many decisions are thought to arise via the accumulation of noisy evidence to a threshold or bound . The family of bounded evidence accumulation models ... offers one such framework for linking choice , reaction time and confidence ... These models depict the decision process as a race between competing accumulators , each of which integrates momentary evidence ... The decision terminates when the accumulated evidence ... reaches a threshold or bound , thereby determining both the choice and the decision time . Confidence ... derives from a mapping between the decision variable and the probability that a decision based on this variable will be correct . The pattern of results in Figure 3B is consistent with the hypothesis that decisions are made when an accumulation of noisy evidence reaches a bound. In the bounded accumulation model, choice, reaction time, and confidence result from accumulating noisy momentary evidence until a decision bound is reached or the stimulus ends.
abstract_sentence: Many decisions arise via the accumulation of noisy evidence to a threshold or bound.

fact: In perception, the mechanism explains the effect of stimulus strength, characterized by signal-to-noise ratio, on decision speed, accuracy and confidence.
source_span: In perception , the mechanism explains the effect of stimulus strength , characterized by signal-to-noise ratio , on decision speed , accuracy and confidence . The noisiness of the momentary evidence causes the DV to wander from its starting point ... Noise is the main determinant of both RT and confidence when signal-to-noise is low , that is when choices are more stochastic ( less accurate ) . The overall quality of the fits—across all tasks and both species—indicates that the influence of motion strength and volatility on choice, reaction time and confidence can be explained by a common mechanism of bounded evidence accumulation.
abstract_sentence: In perception, the accumulation of noisy evidence explains how stimulus strength affects decision speed, accuracy, and confidence.

fact: An increase in noise should lead to faster decisions, reduced accuracy and, paradoxically, higher confidence according to bounded evidence accumulation models.
source_span: An increase in noise should lead to faster decisions , reduced accuracy and , paradoxically , higher confidence . Specifically , were it possible to leave unchanged the expectation of each sample of momentary evidence while boosting the noise associated with it , then the bounded accumulation of the noisier samples should lead to ( i ) lower accuracy when the expectation of the momentary evidence is strong , ( ii ) faster reaction times when the momentary evidence is weak , and ( iii ) increased confidence when the momentary evidence is weak . The important point is that by increasing noise , the volatility manipulation accelerates the dispersion of the decision variable away from its expected value and nearer the termination bounds , hence faster RT. Increased volatility should affect confidence because it mimics an increase in the diffusion rate . At low coherences in particular , its main effect on the DV is to accelerate its exodus away from neutral ( probability correct = 0 . 5 ) to more extreme values . Therefore , we predicted that volatility would increase confidence at low coherences , for the same reason that it speeds the RT.
abstract_sentence: An increase in noise should lead to faster decisions, reduced accuracy, and paradoxically, higher confidence.

fact: The study introduced a novel sensory manipulation that mimics adding unbiased noise to motion-selective regions of visual cortex.
source_span: To test these predictions , we introduce a novel sensory manipulation that mimics the addition of unbiased noise to motion-selective regions of visual cortex , which we verified with neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST . which we verified with neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST . We verified that the manipulation has the desired properties by recording from direction selective neurons in the middle temporal (MT) and medial superior temporal (MST) areas of the macaque visual cortex. Neurons in these areas are known to represent the momentary evidence in tasks identical to those in our study. We therefore sought a method to manipulate the variance associated with the neural representation of momentary evidence without affecting its mean. We achieved this with a manipulation of the motion information in a random dot motion (RDM) display, by adding a second level of randomness which increased its volatility but was unbiased with respect to the strength and direction of motion evidence.
abstract_sentence: The study introduced a novel sensory manipulation that mimics adding unbiased noise to motion-selective regions of visual cortex, verified by neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST.

fact: Increasing the noise induced faster decisions and greater confidence over a range of stimuli for which accuracy was minimally impaired in humans and monkeys.
source_span: For both humans and monkeys , increasing the noise induced faster decisions and greater confidence over a range of stimuli for which accuracy was minimally impaired . The main effect of high volatility was to decrease RTs , particularly at the weakest motion strengths ( Figure 3B , bottom row , red ) . This effect was robust for all three human subjects and the monkey ( Equation 16 , all p<0 . 03 , t-test , H0: β2=0 ) . The manipulation affected the accuracy only subtly , and this was not statistically reliable for individual subjects in the RT task ( Figure 3B , top row; for the four subjects: p=[0 . 35 , 0 . 65 , 0 . 2 , 0 . 26] , Equation 17 , likelihood-ratio test ) . As shown in Figure 4B (lower panel), the proportion of trials the monkey decided to waive the sure-bet option (deciding instead for a riskier direction choice) was greater on the high volatility trials (Equation 19, p<10–6, likelihood-ratio test). Thus, high volatility increased the monkey’s confidence, and did so despite a negligible effect on accuracy.
abstract_sentence: Increasing noise induced faster decisions and greater confidence in both humans and monkeys over a range of stimuli with minimal impairment to accuracy.

fact: The magnitude of the effects was in agreement with predictions of a bounded evidence accumulation model.
source_span: The magnitude of the effects was in agreement with predictions of a bounded evidence accumulation model . ( iii ) showed how a framework based on the bounded accumulation of evidence can account for the joint effect of volatility on choice , reaction time and confidence .
abstract_sentence: The magnitude of the effects of noise on decision speed and confidence matched predictions of a bounded evidence accumulation model.

fact: The deamidase OspI from Shigella flexneri deamidates a glutamine residue in the host ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme UBC13 and converts it to glutamate (Q100E).
source_span: The deamidase OspI from enteric bacteria Shigella flexneri deamidates a glutamine residue in the host ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme UBC13 and converts it to glutamate ( Q100E ) .
abstract_sentence: The bacterial enzyme OspI from Shigella flexneri modifies UBC13 by deamidating glutamine 100 to glutamate.

fact: Its polyubiquitination activity in complex with the RING-finger ubiquitin ligase TRAF6 and the downstream NF-κB inflammatory response is silenced.
source_span: Consequently , its polyubiquitination activity in complex with the RING-finger ubiquitin ligase TRAF6 and the downstream NF-κB inflammatory response is silenced . The Shigella flexneri effector OspI suppresses the inflammatory response (NF-κB pathway) via deamidation of UBC13 at Q100.
abstract_sentence: Deamidation of UBC13 by OspI silences its polyubiquitination activity with TRAF6 and blocks downstream NF-κB inflammatory signaling.

fact: Deamidation inhibits the interaction between UBC13 and TRAF6 RING-domain by perturbing both the native and transient interactions.
source_span: We report that deamidation inhibits the interaction between UBC13 and TRAF6 RING-domain ( TRAF6RING ) by perturbing both the native and transient interactions . Altogether, deamidation inhibited the binding of TRAF6RING to UBC13, but neither changed the fold of UBC13 nor its intrinsic E2 activity. Deamidation of UBC13 reduces its binding affinity to RING domains such as TRAF6RING and RNF38RING. Deamidated UBC13~Ub conjugates fail to bind RING domains such as TRAF6RZ3 and RNF38RING, unlike non-deamidated UBC13~Ub conjugates.
abstract_sentence: Deamidation inhibits the interaction between UBC13 and the TRAF6 RING domain by disrupting both native and transient protein-protein interactions.

fact: Deamidation creates a new intramolecular salt-bridge in UBC13 that competes with a critical intermolecular salt-bridge at the native UBC13/TRAF6RING interface.
source_span: Deamidation creates a new intramolecular salt-bridge in UBC13 that competes with a critical intermolecular salt-bridge at the native UBC13/TRAF6RING interface . An intramolecular salt-bridge was observed between R14 and E100 in dUBC13... The deamidation-induced intramolecular R14/E100 salt-bridge may interfere with the intermolecular R14/E69 salt-bridge to destabilize the complex. The interaction with TRAF6 is inhibited because E100 in dUBC13 competes with an intermolecular R14/E69 salt-bridge at the dUBC13/TRAF6RING interface to form an intramolecular salt-bridge, which destabilizes the native complex. Further studies showed that deamidation disrupts the interaction between UBC13 and TRAF6RING by three mechanisms: i ) A new intramolecular R14/E100 salt-bridge appears in dUBC13 , which competes with a critical intermolecular salt-bridge in the native complex ...
abstract_sentence: Deamidation creates a new intramolecular salt-bridge in UBC13 that competes with a critical intermolecular salt-bridge at the UBC13/TRAF6 interface, weakening their association.

fact: The salt-bridge competition prevents transient interactions necessary to form a typical UBC13/RING complex.
source_span: To summarize , unbiased association simulations indicate that the critical transient contacts formed by R14 were absent in the deamidated complex , presumably due to the salt-bridge competition . The association rate constant reduced by three-fold for dUBC13/TRAF6RING at low salt , indicating that deamidation reduces the association of the transient complex . In the wt complex , a transient attractive interaction was observed between R14 in UBC13 and D57 in TRAF6RING ... However , the R14/D57 interaction was absent in the dUBC13 complex , and it dissociated prematurely . The association and stability dropped by 2 . 3 fold in the dUBC13 complex at low salt , suggesting that deamidation reduces the formation of the native-like transient complex .
abstract_sentence: Salt-bridge competition caused by deamidation prevents transient interactions necessary for forming the typical UBC13/RING complex.

fact: Repulsion between E100 and the negatively charged surface of RING also prevents transient interactions in the UBC13/RING complex.
source_span: Repulsion between E100 and the negatively charged surface of RING also prevents transient interactions in the UBC13/RING complex . Overall , electrostatic repulsion between E100 and the negatively charged interface of TRAF6RING was observed in the dUBC13 transient complexes , which could destabilize it . Substitution at Q100 with a negatively charged residue inhibited the interaction between UBC13 and TRAF6RING... introduction of an additional negative charge in UBC13 upon deamidation could perturb the interfacial electrostatic contacts to disrupt the interaction.
abstract_sentence: Electrostatic repulsion between the negatively charged E100 in deamidated UBC13 and the negatively charged surface of TRAF6 RING domain further reduces transient interactions.

fact: Deamidation perturbs the conformation and stability of transient complexes to inhibit protein-protein association.
source_span: Our study highlights that deamidation of residues that do not directly participate in the E2/E3 interaction but are close to the interface can effectively modulate the interaction by perturbing the native and transient intermolecular contacts . PTMs like phosphorylation, eliminylation, and deamidation can change the surface electrostatics of a protein to modulate the conformation and population of transient complexes significantly. By a combination of all-atom simulations and experimental data, this study provides molecular details of how PTMs can modulate transient protein-protein association to inhibit interaction. This study introduces a new approach to understand the functional role of PTMs by considering their transient interactions.
abstract_sentence: Post-translational modifications like deamidation can regulate protein-protein transient interactions by perturbing native and transient contacts, affecting signaling pathways.

fact: Working memory is supported by coordinated interactions among large-scale distributed brain networks, particularly involving frontal and parietal regions.
source_span: Cognitive functions such as working memory ( WM ) are emergent properties of large-scale network interactions ... Frontal and parietal brain regions support WM ( Cohen et al . , 1997; Prabhakaran et al . , 2000; Pessoa et al . , 2002; Todd and Marois , 2004 ) .
abstract_sentence: Working memory depends on coordinated interactions among large-scale brain networks, especially frontal and parietal regions.

fact: Oscillatory activity in the theta frequency range (4–8 Hz) organizes neuronal ensembles across distant brain regions during working memory processes.
source_span: Oscillatory activity in the theta range ( 4–8 Hz ) appears to organize local neuronal ensembles across distant regions during WM processes ( Buzsáki , 1996; Sarnthein et al . , 1998; Rutishauser et al . , 2010 ) . Increased rhythmic synchrony across a network is thought to improve information processing by increasing network efficiency , an effect particularly important during demanding cognitive processing ( Fries , 2005 , 2009; Deco et al . , 2011 ) .
abstract_sentence: Oscillatory brain activity, especially in the theta frequency range, helps coordinate distant brain regions during working memory.

fact: Causal evidence for how oscillatory activity shapes network dynamics and behavior in humans is limited.
source_span: However , causal evidence for the way oscillatory activity shapes network dynamics and behavior in humans is limited .
abstract_sentence: There is limited causal evidence in humans for how oscillatory activity shapes brain network dynamics and behavior.

fact: The study applied transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) to modulate oscillatory activity in a right frontoparietal network supporting working memory.
source_span: Here we applied transcranial alternating current stimulation ( tACS ) to exogenously modulate oscillatory activity in a right frontoparietal network that supports WM . Theta ( 6 Hz ) tACS was applied to the middle frontal gyrus and inferior parietal lobule nodes ( center electrode locations at F4 and P4 ) of the frontoparietal network in synchronous ( 0° relative phase ) and desynchronous ( 180° relative phase ) conditions tACS interacts with ongoing oscillations and the resultant neural modulations spread along brain networks ( Fröhlich and McCormick , 2010; Ali et al . , 2013 )
abstract_sentence: The study used transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) to externally modulate oscillatory activity in a right frontoparietal network supporting working memory.

fact: Synchronous (in-phase) tACS stimulation improved working memory performance when cognitive demands were high.
source_span: Externally induced synchronization improved performance when cognitive demands were high . Synchronous tACS improved reaction times ( RTs ) for the more demanding 2-back condition compared both to desynchronous tACS and sham . We replicate the observation that synchronous tACS applied across the frontoparietal networks improves WM performance ( Polanía et al . , 2012 ) , and extend these results by showing that this cognitive enhancement is dependent on the demands of the cognitive task. Remarkably , synchronous tACS produced sufficient improvement in response times to make 2-back performance similar to the 1-back condition , which is typically associated with much faster responses.
abstract_sentence: Externally induced synchronization via tACS improved working memory performance when cognitive demands were high.

fact: Simultaneous fMRI data showed that tACS effects on brain activity depend on the relative phase of stimulation and the internal cognitive processing state.
source_span: Simultaneously collected fMRI data reveals tACS effects dependent on the relative phase of the stimulation and the internal cognitive processing state . In Experiment 2 we use simultaneous tACS-fMRI to investigate the neural correlates of the phase dependent effects of tACS . TACS was employed as a causal ‘physiological probe’ in an experimental design optimized to detect neurophysiological changes associated with the external stimulation . Our results demonstrate that external manipulations of oscillatory synchrony across a right-sided frontoparietal network impact neural activity and modify behavior . The effects depend on the relative phase of the external oscillators and also the underlying cognitive state at the time tACS is applied . Our imaging results for the 2-back and CRT tasks strongly support these notions and show how the physiological effect of external oscillatory manipulations are highly dependent on the underlying cognitive state.
abstract_sentence: tACS effects on brain activity depend on the relative phase of stimulation and the internal cognitive processing state, as shown by simultaneous fMRI.

fact: Synchronous tACS during the verbal WM task increased parietal activity, which correlated with behavioral performance improvements.
source_span: Specifically , synchronous tACS during the verbal WM task increased parietal activity , which correlated with behavioral performance . In keeping with these findings , we show that increased activity within the right inferior parietal lobe correlated with faster responses during the 2-back , supporting a link between neural activity and the behavioral effects of tACS . Furthermore , during maintenance of items in WM the parietal cortex is positively associated with trial-by-trial performance and inter-individual differences in WM capacity ( Todd and Marois , 2004; Xu and Chun , 2006 ) .
abstract_sentence: Synchronous tACS during a verbal working memory task increased parietal brain activity, which correlated with better behavioral performance.

fact: Functional connectivity within the working memory network is modulated by the relative phase of frontoparietal stimulation, influencing information flow.
source_span: Furthermore , functional connectivity results indicate that the relative phase of frontoparietal stimulation influences information flow within the WM network . The functional connectivity of the inferior parietal lobe was also modulated by tACS in a phase dependent manner . Frontal interactions increased with synchronous theta stimulation whereas posterior interactions increased with desynchronous stimulation ... Our results extend these findings by showing how externally induced theta synchrony can increase frontoparietal interactions between the parietal cortex and DLPFC that are important for WM processing . While synchronous stimulation resulted in increased functional connectivity between parietal and frontal areas , desynchronous tACS was associated with increased connectivity to occipital regions , which could suggest an increase in information exchange between higher- and low-level areas .
abstract_sentence: The relative phase of frontoparietal stimulation modulates functional connectivity and information flow within the working memory network.

fact: The study found a direct link between behavioral performance in a demanding working-memory task and large-scale brain synchronization across a right frontoparietal network activated by the task.
source_span: Overall , our findings indicate a direct link between behavioral performance in a demanding working-memory task and large-scale brain synchronization across a right frontoparietal network activated by the task . supporting a role for phase synchronization during demanding WM processes and ruling out a simple motor effect . Therefore , we provide a direct demonstration of the role of phase synchronization in cognitive demanding WM processes and we showed the neural correlates associated with this process .
abstract_sentence: There is a direct link between behavioral performance in demanding working memory tasks and large-scale brain synchronization across a right frontoparietal network.

fact: The granular retrosplenial cortex (RSG) is critical for both spatial and non-spatial behaviors.
source_span: The granular retrosplenial cortex ( RSG ) is critical for both spatial and non-spatial behaviors , but the underlying neural codes remain poorly understood .
abstract_sentence: The granular retrosplenial cortex (RSG) is critical for both spatial and non-spatial behaviors.

fact: Channelrhodopsin-assisted circuit mapping (CRACM) was used to study subtype-specific circuits formed by anterior thalamic, claustral, anterior cingulate, and dorsal subicular inputs to the RSG.
source_span: Here , we use channelrhodopsin ( ChR2 ) -assisted circuit mapping ( CRACM ) to study the subtype-specific circuits formed by anterior thalamic , claustral , anterior cingulate , and dorsal subicular inputs to the RSG .
abstract_sentence: Optogenetic circuit mapping in mice reveals parallel circuits in superficial RSG that process different inputs.

fact: The anterior thalamus and dorsal subiculum provide spatial information inputs that selectively recruit low-rheobase (LR) pyramidal cells in the superficial layers of the RSG.
source_span: The anterior thalamus and dorsal subiculum , sources of spatial information , strongly and selectively recruit small low-rheobase ( LR ) pyramidal cells in RSG . Specifically , we find that anterior thalamus and dorsal subiculum preferentially control LR neurons , whereas claustrum and anterior cingulate control RS cells . Thus , inputs from both the dorsal subiculum and anterior thalamus target LR cells , reflecting their precise overlap with LR dendrites , while the claustrum and anterior cingulate cortex instead target RS cells . These anatomical results mirror our functional findings that LR neurons are preferentially driven by both ADAV and DS inputs, while RS neurons are targeted by CLA and ACC inputs.
abstract_sentence: Anterior thalamus and dorsal subiculum inputs provide spatial information and selectively recruit low-rheobase (LR) pyramidal cells in superficial RSG.

fact: Claustral and anterior cingulate inputs, which carry mostly non-spatial information, preferentially control neighboring regular-spiking (RS) pyramidal cells in the superficial RSG.
source_span: In contrast , neighboring regular-spiking ( RS ) cells are preferentially controlled by claustral and anterior cingulate inputs , sources of mostly non-spatial information . Dendritic lamination plots of LR and RS dendrites and projection density plots of CLA axons and terminal arbors show that RS , but not LR , apical dendrites anatomically overlap with CLA arbors in superficial layers 1 c and two and upper layer 5. We found that RS neurons have significantly larger responses to CLA input compared to LR neurons when stimulated at layer 1/2 , the area of the strongest superficial projection density of CLA arbors. Similarly , layer 5 RS neurons exhibited significantly larger EPSP amplitudes in response to CLA inputs compared to LR cells.
abstract_sentence: Neighboring regular-spiking (RS) pyramidal cells in superficial RSG are preferentially controlled by claustral and anterior cingulate inputs, which carry mostly non-spatial information.

fact: Precise sublaminar axonal and dendritic arborization within layer 1 of the RSG permits parallel processing of spatial and non-spatial inputs.
source_span: Precise sublaminar axonal and dendritic arborization within RSG layer 1 , in particular , permits this parallel processing . Thus , the connectivity between anterior thalamic TC arbors and L3 principal neurons in RSG highlights a circuit that depends on the precise sublaminar colocalization of both local principal cells’ dendrites and incoming thalamocortical axons. This lamination of functional responses in the RS cell precisely aligns with the lamination of ClaC axons and terminal arbors. This again indicates that parallel circuits in RSG process TC versus ClaC and CC information , and this parallel processing is enabled by precise sublaminar organization of afferent axons and layer three principal cell apical dendrites .
abstract_sentence: Precise sublaminar axonal and dendritic arborization within layer 1 of the RSG permits parallel processing of spatial and non-spatial inputs.

fact: Thalamocortical synaptic dynamics enable low-rheobase (LR) neurons in the RSG to compute the speed of head rotation despite receiving head direction inputs that do not explicitly encode speed.
source_span: Observed thalamocortical synaptic dynamics enable computational models of LR neurons to compute the speed of head rotation , despite receiving head direction inputs that do not explicitly encode speed . We show that the synaptic dynamics of thalamic inputs allow for the robust encoding of angular speed by LR cell models , even though these inputs only explicitly contain information about head direction , not speed. We found that the firing rate of the postsynaptic LR cell receiving HD input via depressing synapses was strongly correlated with angular head speed, giving rise to symmetrical angular head velocity tuning. Taken together, these results suggest that synaptic depression of HD ensemble inputs introduces an angular head speed signal into the LR population, producing neurons that are more responsive during faster head turns, and potentially supporting the spatial orientation encoding functions attributed to the RSG.
abstract_sentence: Thalamocortical synaptic dynamics enable low-rheobase (LR) neurons in the RSG to compute the speed of head rotation despite receiving head direction inputs that do not explicitly encode speed.

fact: Parallel input streams identify low-rheobase (LR) pyramidal neurons as a distinct principal neuronal subtype ideally positioned to support spatial orientation computations in the RSG.
source_span: Thus , parallel input streams identify a distinct principal neuronal subtype ideally positioned to support spatial orientation computations in the RSG . Together , our results suggest that LR neurons are ideally positioned to contribute to the initial spatial orientation computations performed in superficial RSG.
abstract_sentence: Parallel input streams identify low-rheobase (LR) pyramidal neurons as a distinct principal neuronal subtype ideally positioned to support spatial orientation computations in the RSG.

fact: Petal number is a robust trait in flowering plants, usually invariant within species and higher taxonomic orders, likely due to stabilizing selection.
source_span: Petal number is a robust trait in flowering plants and usually invariant within species and even higher taxonomic orders… suggesting that this trait was canalized during angiosperm evolution to produce a stable phenotype in the face of genetic and environmental perturbation. Petals are usually required to open the flower and to help attract pollinators… therefore a stable number of petals could ensure a reliable display of the reproductive organs and a reproducible cue for pollinators. Developmental systems are remarkably robust to natural perturbations, such that individuals tend to develop normally despite variation in the environment or their genetic make-up.
abstract_sentence: Invariant floral forms are important for reproductive success and robust to natural perturbations.

fact: Petal number is invariant among natural accessions of Arabidopsis thaliana, reflecting robustness to genetic variation.
source_span: Petal number is invariant among natural accessions of A. thaliana, reflecting its robustness to genetic variation. However, we could change A. thaliana petal number to variable by complementing ap1 mutants with the AP1 genomic locus from C. hirsuta. These flowers mimicked the variable petal number found in C. hirsuta. The flowers of A . thaliana and other Brassicaceae species are readily distinguished by their four petals . This phenotype is robust to natural genetic variation; for example , flowers from genetically diverse A . thaliana accessions consistently produce four petals
abstract_sentence: Petal number is invariant in Arabidopsis thaliana flowers.

fact: Petal number is invariant in Arabidopsis thaliana flowers but varies in the closely related species Cardamine hirsuta.
source_span: Petal number, for example, is invariant in Arabidopsis thaliana flowers. However, petal number varies in the closely related species Cardamine hirsuta, and the genetic basis for this difference between species is unknown. Cardamine hirsuta flowers display a variable number of petals, between zero and four, on a single plant… This phenotype varies in response to both environmental and genetic perturbation. C . hirsuta lacks this robustness and shows variation in petal number . For example , we found similar frequencies of each petal number between zero and four in flowers from 39 C . hirsuta accessions sampled from across the species range
abstract_sentence: Petal number varies in the closely related species Cardamine hirsuta, unlike in Arabidopsis thaliana.

fact: Divergence in the floral regulator APETALA1 (AP1) can account for the species-specific difference in petal number robustness.
source_span: Here we show that divergence in the pleiotropic floral regulator APETALA1 (AP1) can account for the species-specific difference in petal number robustness. In this study, we identified AP1 as a gene of major effect in the evolutionary transition from a robust phenotype of four petals, typified by A. thaliana, to a variable petal number in C. hirsuta.
abstract_sentence: Divergence in the floral regulator APETALA1 (AP1) explains the species-specific difference in petal number robustness between Arabidopsis thaliana and Cardamine hirsuta.

fact: A. thaliana AP1 confers robustness by masking the phenotypic expression of quantitative trait loci controlling petal number in C. hirsuta.
source_span: This large effect of AP1 is explained by epistatic interactions: A. thaliana AP1 confers robustness by masking the phenotypic expression of quantitative trait loci controlling petal number in C. hirsuta. the allelic effects of these 9 QTL were undetectable in the presence of the A . thaliana AP1 genomic locus ... Thus , A . thaliana AP1 canalized C . hirsuta petal number by masking the phenotypic effects of at least 9 QTL . We mapped this natural variation to specific QTL in the C. hirsuta genome and showed that introducing the A. thaliana AP1 locus masked the effects of all QTL. Therefore, petal number was effectively canalized in C. hirsuta via epistasis of A. thaliana AP1 over existing QTL.
abstract_sentence: Arabidopsis thaliana AP1 confers robustness in petal number by masking the effects of quantitative trait loci controlling petal number in Cardamine hirsuta.

fact: C. hirsuta AP1 fails to complement this function of A. thaliana AP1, conferring variable petal number, and upstream regulatory regions of AP1 contribute to this divergence.
source_span: We show that C. hirsuta AP1 fails to complement this function of A. thaliana AP1, conferring variable petal number. …and that upstream regulatory regions of AP1 contribute to this divergence. We found that AP1 genes from A. thaliana and C. hirsuta diverged in their ability to specify an invariant number of four petals. This difference mapped broadly to upstream regulatory rather than coding regions of AP1, and did not alter the function of AP1 in flower initiation or sepal specification.
abstract_sentence: Cardamine hirsuta AP1 fails to complement the function of Arabidopsis thaliana AP1, resulting in variable petal number, and upstream regulatory regions of AP1 contribute to this divergence.

fact: Petal number variation in Cardamine hirsuta is maintained despite sufficient genetic variation in natural populations to produce four-petalled flowers.
source_span: Moreover, variable petal number is maintained in C. hirsuta despite sufficient standing genetic variation in natural accessions to produce plants with four-petalled flowers. These recombinant inbred populations contained a high frequency of lines with high average petal numbers, including four petals... This shows that there is sufficient standing genetic variation to produce phenotypes through recombination that are not observed in natural accessions.
abstract_sentence: Variable petal number is maintained in Cardamine hirsuta despite sufficient standing genetic variation to produce four-petalled flowers.

fact: Proper function and repair of the digestive system are vital to most animals.
source_span: Proper function and repair of the digestive system are vital to most animals.
abstract_sentence: Proper function and repair of the digestive system are vital to most animals.

fact: Deciphering the mechanisms involved in digestive system function and repair requires an atlas of gene expression and cell types.
source_span: Deciphering the mechanisms involved in these processes requires an atlas of gene expression and cell types. characterization of an organ’s composition and gene expression at a cellular level in the uninjured state is an essential step in unraveling the mechanisms required for faithful re-establishment of organ morphology and physiology.
abstract_sentence: Deciphering the mechanisms involved in digestive system function and repair requires an atlas of gene expression and cell types.

fact: The planarian flatworm Schmidtea mediterranea can regenerate all organs, including the gut, and was studied using laser-capture microdissection and RNA-seq to characterize its intestinal transcriptome.
source_span: Here , we applied laser-capture microdissection ( LCM ) and RNA-seq to characterize the intestinal transcriptome of Schmidtea mediterranea , a planarian flatworm that can regenerate all organs , including the gut. Here , we report the application of LCM for expression profiling of the planarian intestine . We first identified appropriate tissue-processing conditions for extraction of intact RNA from planarian tissue sections . Then , using RNA-Seq , bioinformatics approaches , and whole-mount in situ hybridization , we characterized the intestinal transcriptome . Development of a robust method for isolating intestinal tissue , and characterization of the intestinal transcriptome , will facilitate mechanistic studies in planarians .
abstract_sentence: Laser-capture microdissection and RNA sequencing were used to characterize the intestinal transcriptome of Schmidtea mediterranea, a planarian flatworm that can regenerate all organs including the gut.

fact: The study identified hundreds of intestine-expressed genes not found by earlier methods.
source_span: We identified hundreds of genes with intestinal expression undetected by previous approaches. Furthermore, we identified 809 intestine-enriched transcripts that single-cell studies did not find to be enriched in the intestine (or for some, any planarian cell type). the detection of transcripts exclusively enriched in laser-captured intestine suggests that expression profiling of laser-captured bulk tissue is more sensitive than current single-cell profiling approaches , and that LCM may be a preferable method for assessing tissue-specific gene expression when single-cell resolution is not required .
abstract_sentence: Hundreds of genes with intestinal expression in Schmidtea mediterranea were identified that were undetected by previous approaches.

fact: Planarian digestive physiology and cell types are extensively conserved with those of other animals, including humans.
source_span: Systematic analyses revealed extensive conservation of digestive physiology and cell types with other animals , including humans. we found that the intestine expresses numerous homologs of transcripts that are enriched in human GI tissues The intestine expresses genes involved in metabolism , nutrient storage and transport , innate immunity , and other physiological roles , demonstrating considerable functional homology with digestive systems of other animals , including humans . our results suggest broad similarity between planarians and other animals with respect to evolutionarily conserved signaling pathways that govern cell dynamics in the digestive tract
abstract_sentence: The digestive physiology and cell types of Schmidtea mediterranea show extensive conservation with other animals, including humans.

fact: Spatial LCM uncovered regional differences in gene expression along the medio-lateral axis of the planarian intestine, notably in goblet cells.
source_span: Furthermore , spatial LCM enabled us to uncover previously unappreciated regionalization of gene expression in the planarian intestine along the medio-lateral axis , especially among intestinal goblet cells. Some goblet-cell-specific transcripts show regional enrichment along the mediolateral axis of the intestine, suggesting functional specialization within this cell type. We discovered previously unappreciated regionalization and diversity of intestinal cell types and subtypes , especially amongst goblet cells , and hundreds of intestine-enriched transcripts not identified in recent single-cell profiling efforts . Although most (1,531/1,844) transcripts were upregulated in both medial and lateral intestine, a small subset of transcripts was significantly upregulated only in medial (217/1,844) or lateral (96/1,844) intestine.
abstract_sentence: Spatial laser-capture microdissection revealed previously unappreciated regionalization of gene expression along the medio-lateral axis of the planarian intestine, especially among intestinal goblet cells.

fact: The transcription factors gli-1 and RREB2 regulate regeneration and maintenance of goblet cells in the planarian intestine.
source_span: Finally , we identified two intestine-enriched transcription factors that specifically regulate regeneration ( hedgehog signaling effector gli-1 ) or maintenance ( RREB2 ) of goblet cells. Knockdown of a second transcription factor , gli-1 ... caused failure of goblet cells to regenerate at the midline of the new anterior branch ... goblet cells were less abundant in pre-existing regions of the intestine , particularly in lateral intestinal branches while RREB2 may control maintenance or survival of goblet cells after they initially differentiate Together , these results suggest that gli-1 regulates neoblast fate specification and/or differentiation of neoblast progeny into goblet cells in new intestinal branches
abstract_sentence: Two intestine-enriched transcription factors, gli-1 and RREB2, specifically regulate regeneration or maintenance of goblet cells in Schmidtea mediterranea.

fact: This work provides resources for further investigation of mechanisms involved in gastrointestinal function, repair, and regeneration.
source_span: The planarian intestinal transcriptome is a foundational resource for investigating numerous aspects of intestine regeneration and physiology . To facilitate exploration of the planarian intestinal transcriptome as a resource , we have developed a website , plangut . omrf . org The methods and resources presented here will also support comparative analyses , complementing current and future efforts to understand digestive tract regeneration in platyhelminths , sea cucumbers , annelids , ascidians , amphibians , and mammals ... In addition , studies in planarians and other regeneration models are likely to generate new insights into cellular processes ( e . g . proliferation , differentiation , metabolism , and stress responses ) whose dysregulation underlies human gastrointestinal pathologies associated with aging and disease .
abstract_sentence: The planarian intestinal transcriptome resource supports further investigation of gastrointestinal function, repair, and regeneration.

fact: Mitochondria are essential to cellular bioenergetics and metabolism, making quality control mechanisms that dispose of damaged mitochondrial proteins vital for cellular function.
source_span: Proper protein folding is essential for organelle and cell homeostasis . Proteins may fail to achieve or retain their functional conformations due to genetic or environmental insults and cells have evolved elaborate protein quality control ( QC ) mechanisms to combat misfolding . QC systems recognize and refold misfolded proteins and , when not possible , sequester or degrade them to prevent their often deleterious accumulation ( Kevei et al . , 2017 ) . Mitochondrial proteins are subject to ongoing oxidative insults that can result in damage , misfolding , and dysfunction . Mitochondria require mechanisms to eliminate these proteins to maintain organellar integrity and essential functions ( Voos et al . , 2016 ) . Mitochondria are essential to cellular bioenergetics and metabolism . It is therefore vital that QC mechanisms dispose of damaged proteins that can compromise function .
abstract_sentence: Maintaining mitochondrial function requires mechanisms to recognize and remove misfolded proteins.

fact: Quality control pathways for misfolded mitochondrial proteins are poorly defined.
source_span: However , quality control ( QC ) pathways for misfolded mitochondrial proteins remain poorly defined . Thus , a universal MAD pathway for MOM proteins has not been described and many steps in substrate degradation remain unexamined .
abstract_sentence: Quality control pathways for misfolded mitochondrial proteins are poorly defined.

fact: Temperature-sensitive peripheral mitochondrial outer membrane proteins sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts were established as quality control substrates to study mitochondrial degradation.
source_span: Here , we establish temperature-sensitive ( ts- ) peripheral mitochondrial outer membrane ( MOM ) proteins as novel model QC substrates in Saccharomyces cerevisiae . In this study , we establish temperature-sensitive ( ts- ) peripheral MOM proteins ( sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts ) as QC substrates . While previous mitochondrial UPS substrates have consisted primarily of native proteins ... sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts contain mutations that render them unstable at the non-permissive temperature , and thus mimic damaged , misfolded proteins .
abstract_sentence: Temperature-sensitive peripheral mitochondrial outer membrane proteins were established as novel model quality control substrates in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

fact: The ts- proteins sen2-1HAts and sam35-2HAts are degraded from the MOM by the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
source_span: The ts- proteins sen2-1HAts and sam35-2HAts are degraded from the MOM by the ubiquitin-proteasome system . Here , we define a UPS-mediated pathway for the degradation of individual dysfunctional yeast MOM proteins using two newly-established model QC substrates , sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts ( schematized in Figure 7 ) . Such degradation frequently occurs via the ubiquitin-proteasome system ( UPS ) , where substrates are modified with ubiquitin leading to their destruction by the 26S proteasome ( Metzger et al . , 2012 ) . While there is no evidence for proteasomes inside mitochondria , the mitochondrial outer membrane ( MOM ) is fully accessible to cytosolic proteasomes .
abstract_sentence: The temperature-sensitive proteins sen2-1HAts and sam35-2HAts are degraded from the mitochondrial outer membrane by the ubiquitin-proteasome system.

fact: Ubiquitination of sen2-1HAts is mediated by the ubiquitin ligase ( E3 ) Ubr1 , while sam35-2HAts is ubiquitinated primarily by San1 .
source_span: Ubiquitination of sen2-1HAts is mediated by the ubiquitin ligase ( E3 ) Ubr1 , while sam35-2HAts is ubiquitinated primarily by San1 . We found that san1Δ impaired turnover of sam35-2HAts ... while ubr1Δ impaired turnover of sen2-1HAts ... Loss of Ubr1 in conjunction with san1Δ led to greater stabilization than loss of San1 alone ... indicating that Ubr1 can target sam35-2HAts in the absence of San1 . These results establish that San1 and Ubr1 can function as components of the MAD machinery for proteasome-mediated degradation of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts, respectively. Instead , San1 and Ubr1 , which have broad roles as quality control E3s for misfolded cytosolic and nuclear proteins ... , are required to degrade mitochondrial ts- substrates . ... we find no evidence for the involvement of Rsp5 or SCFMdm30 ubiquitin ligases ...
abstract_sentence: Ubiquitination of sen2-1HAts is mediated by the ubiquitin ligase Ubr1, while sam35-2HAts is ubiquitinated primarily by San1.

fact: Mitochondria-associated degradation ( MAD ) of both substrates requires the SSA family of Hsp70s and the Hsp40 Sis1 , providing the first evidence for chaperone involvement in MAD .
source_span: Mitochondria-associated degradation ( MAD ) of both substrates requires the SSA family of Hsp70s and the Hsp40 Sis1 , providing the first evidence for chaperone involvement in MAD . Both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts were strongly stabilized in a conditional yeast strain where three SSA family members are deleted and the fourth (SSA1) is ts- (ssa1-45ts; ssa1-45ts ssa2Δ ssa3Δ ssa4Δ) relative to the control strain (SSA1; SSA1 ssa2Δ ssa3Δ ssa4Δ; Figure 4A). Depletion of ~90% of Sis1 protein using Sis1 DAmP cells slowed the turnover of both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts, while loss of Ydj1 or its ortholog, Hlj1, did not. Notably, the SSA1 chaperone was also required for ubiquitination: despite the accumulation of unmodified sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts, ubiquitin-modified forms are dramatically reduced when SSA1 is inactivated (Figure 4C).
abstract_sentence: Mitochondria-associated degradation of both substrates requires the SSA family of Hsp70 chaperones and the Hsp40 Sis1, providing the first evidence for chaperone involvement in mitochondria-associated degradation.

fact: The Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 AAA-ATPase complex, Doa1, and a mitochondrial pool of the transmembrane Cdc48 adaptor Ubx2 are implicated in their degradation.
source_span: In addition to a role for the Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 AAA-ATPase complex , Doa1 and a mitochondrial pool of the transmembrane Cdc48 adaptor , Ubx2 , are implicated in their degradation . All together, these results indicate that ubiquitinated mitochondrial QC substrates require the Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 complex for efficient proteasomal degradation. Notably, only the loss of Ubx2 significantly stabilized sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts. We also confirmed this by co-localization of Ubx2-GFP with both ER (Sec63-RFP) and mitochondrial (mtRFP) markers by microscopy... The mitochondrial localization of a portion of Ubx2 was further verified biochemically by isolation of mitochondria.
abstract_sentence: The Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 AAA-ATPase complex, Doa1, and a mitochondrial pool of the transmembrane Cdc48 adaptor Ubx2 are implicated in the degradation of these mitochondrial outer membrane proteins.

fact: This study reveals a unique QC pathway comprised of a combination of cytosolic and mitochondrial factors that distinguish it from other cellular QC pathways.
source_span: This study reveals a unique QC pathway comprised of a combination of cytosolic and mitochondrial factors that distinguish it from other cellular QC pathways . These new mitochondrial model substrates have revealed a tightly-coupled degradation pathway at the MOM that requires both cytosolic and mitochondrial machinery . This MAD QC pathway ... is also not identical to any other cellular QC pathway , although there are points of intersection . Our results reveal a requirement for factors not previously implicated in the degradation of native MAD substrates and the combination of components identified defines a distinct QC pathway . The MAD QC pathway characterized here is distinct from this pathway: ts- substrates remain mitochondrial and are degraded independently of ERAD E2s or E3s .
abstract_sentence: This study reveals a unique quality control pathway for misfolded mitochondrial outer membrane proteins that involves both cytosolic and mitochondrial factors and is distinct from other cellular quality control pathways.

fact: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are conserved noncoding RNAs that regulate gene expression posttranscriptionally; miR-9 is one of the most abundant microRNAs in the developing and adult brain.
source_span: MicroRNAs ( miRNAs ) are conserved noncoding RNAs that function as posttranscriptional regulators of gene expression . Importantly , miR-9 is one of the most abundant miRNAs in the developing and adult brain ( Lagos-Quintana et al . , 2002; Krichevsky et al . , 2003 ) .
abstract_sentence: MicroRNAs are conserved noncoding RNAs that regulate gene expression posttranscriptionally, and miR-9 is one of the most abundant microRNAs in the brain.

fact: The role of miR-9 in dendritic and synaptic development in differentiated neurons was largely unknown before this study.
source_span: Although the function of miR-9 has been well characterized in neural progenitors , its role in dendritic and synaptic development remains largely unknown .
abstract_sentence: The role of miR-9 in dendritic and synaptic development in differentiated neurons was largely unknown before this study.

fact: The researchers developed a transgenic miRNA sponge mouse line that allows conditional and spatio-temporal inactivation of the miR-9 family in vivo.
source_span: In order to target miR-9 in vivo , we developed a transgenic miRNA sponge mouse line allowing conditional inactivation of the miR-9 family in a spatio-temporal-controlled manner . In summary , we describe the first transgenic sponge mouse line that allows for conditional inactivation of an miRNA family in a spatio-temporal-controlled manner . Here , we describe for the first time a conditional transgenic sponge mouse model . We derived two different strains for in vivo analysis: ( i ) a reporter mouse line to monitor miR-9 activity with single-cell resolution and ( ii ) a line for miR-9 loss-of-function studies . To address the impact of miR-9 loss of function on dendritic growth in vivo, we generated a miR-9-SpNestin-Cre mouse line by breeding miR-9-Spfl-Stop mice with the Nestin-Cre mouse line. This newly generated mouse line conditionally expresses the GFP-FC-miR-9-sponge in the CNS.
abstract_sentence: A transgenic miRNA sponge mouse line was developed to conditionally inactivate the miR-9 family in a spatio-temporal controlled manner in vivo.

fact: Using the miRNA sponge mouse model, the study found that miR-9 controls dendritic growth and synaptic transmission in vivo.
source_span: Using this novel approach , we found that miR-9 controls dendritic growth and synaptic transmission in vivo . Pyramidal CA1 neurons from miR-9-SpNestin-Cre mice exhibited a reduction in total dendritic length and arborization complexity compared to control littermates (miR-9-Spfl-Stop). fEPSP recordings in acute hippocampal brain slices demonstrate an impairment of synaptic transmission... Input–output curve showing reduced synaptic transmission and reduced excitability in miR-9-SpNestin-Cre slices.
abstract_sentence: Using the miRNA sponge mouse model, miR-9 was found to control dendritic growth and synaptic transmission in vivo.

fact: miR-9 mediates downregulation of the transcriptional repressor REST, which is essential for proper dendritic growth.
source_span: Furthermore , we demonstrate that miR-9-mediated downregulation of the transcriptional repressor REST is essential for proper dendritic growth . We found that 13 out of 26 miR-9 predicted targets were upregulated in miR-9-SpNestin-Cre neurons. Interestingly, one of the upregulated mRNAs encodes the global transcriptional repressor element 1 (RE-1) silencing transcription factor (REST/NRSF). Importantly, we also found elevated REST protein levels in sponge expressing neurons. We observed that shREST transfection strongly rescued the dendritic growth defects in miR-9-SpNestin-Cre neurons, indicating that increased REST level is indeed the major mediator of miR-9 effects on dendritic growth.
abstract_sentence: miR-9 mediates downregulation of the transcriptional repressor REST, which is essential for proper dendritic growth.

fact: Thermal biology predicts that vector-borne disease transmission peaks at intermediate temperatures and declines at high and low temperatures.
source_span: Thermal biology predicts that vector-borne disease transmission peaks at intermediate temperatures and declines at high and low temperatures. RRV incidence is often positively associated with warmer temperatures, but this relationship varies across space and time due to an intermediate thermal optimum for transmission. High temperatures can constrain RRV transmission and mosquito populations, with outbreaks less likely when there are more days above 35°C and mosquito populations peaking around 25°C but declining above 32°C.
abstract_sentence: Vector-borne disease transmission peaks at intermediate temperatures and declines at high and low temperatures.

fact: Thermal optima and limits remain unknown for most vector-borne pathogens.
source_span: However , thermal optima and limits remain unknown for most vector-borne pathogens.
abstract_sentence: Thermal optima and limits remain unknown for most vector-borne pathogens.

fact: We built a mechanistic model for the thermal response of Ross River virus, an important mosquito-borne pathogen in Australia, Pacific Islands, and potentially at risk of emerging worldwide.
source_span: We built a mechanistic model for the thermal response of Ross River virus , an important mosquito-borne pathogen in Australia , Pacific Islands , and potentially at risk of emerging worldwide. Our main model ( ‘full R0 Model , ’ Equation 1 ) assumes temperature drives mosquito density and includes the relevant life history trait thermal responses ( Parham and Michael , 2009; Mordecai et al . , 2013; Mordecai et al . , 2017 ) . We calculated R0 ( T ) at 0 . 2°C increments and projected it onto the landscape for monthly mean temperatures from WorldClim data at a 5 min resolution ( approximately 10 km2 at the equator ) .
abstract_sentence: A mechanistic model was built to describe the thermal response of Ross River virus transmission.

fact: Transmission peaks at moderate temperatures (26.4°C) and declines to zero at thermal limits (17.0 and 31.5°C).
source_span: Transmission peaks at moderate temperatures ( 26 . 4°C ) and declines to zero at thermal limits ( 17 . 0 and 31 . 5°C ) . Transmission potential ( relative R0 from the full R0 model ) peaked at 26 . 4°C , and was positive from 17 . 0–31 . 5°C ( Figure 3 ) . The optimal temperature for transmission is moderate ( 26–27°C; Figure 3 ) , and largely determined by the thermal response of adult mosquito lifespan ( Figure 3—figure supplement 2 ) .
abstract_sentence: Ross River virus transmission peaks at moderate temperatures around 26.4°C and declines to zero below 17.0°C and above 31.5°C.

fact: The model accurately predicts that transmission is year-round endemic in the tropics but seasonal in temperate areas, resulting in the nationwide seasonal peak in human cases.
source_span: The model accurately predicts that transmission is year-round endemic in the tropics but seasonal in temperate areas , resulting in the nationwide seasonal peak in human cases . Temperature suitability for RRV transmission varies seasonally across Australia, with temperate regions experiencing seasonal transmission and tropical regions having year-round suitability. RRV is endemic year-round in tropical Australia but shows seasonal epidemics in subtropical and temperate regions due to temperature variation.
abstract_sentence: The model predicts Ross River virus transmission is year-round in tropical areas but seasonal in temperate areas, matching observed human case patterns.

fact: Climate warming will likely increase transmission in temperate areas (where most Australians live) but decrease transmission in tropical areas where mean temperatures are already near the thermal optimum.
source_span: Climate warming will likely increase transmission in temperate areas ( where most Australians live ) but decrease transmission in tropical areas where mean temperatures are already near the thermal optimum . Climate warming will likely increase the geographic and seasonal range of transmission potential in temperate , southern Australia where most Australians live . However , climate change will likely decrease transmission potential in tropical areas like Darwin , where moderate warming ( ~3°C ) would push temperatures above the upper thermal limit for transmission for most of the year ( Figure 5 ) .
abstract_sentence: Climate warming is likely to increase Ross River virus transmission in temperate areas but decrease it in tropical areas already near the thermal optimum.

fact: A nonlinear mechanistic model is critical for estimating temperature impacts on transmission because the effect of increasing temperature by a few degrees can have a positive, negligible, or negative impact on R0 along different parts of the thermal response curve.
source_span: A nonlinear mechanistic model is critical for estimating temperature impacts on transmission because the effect of increasing temperature by a few degrees can have a positive , negligible , or negative impact on R0 along different parts of the thermal response curve . Nonlinear thermal responses are particularly important for predicting how transmission will change under future climate regimes .
abstract_sentence: Nonlinear mechanistic models are essential to accurately estimate temperature impacts on Ross River virus transmission.

fact: Motor cortical beta oscillations have been observed for decades, but their specific behavioral correlates remain unclear.
source_span: Motor cortical beta oscillations have been reported for decades , yet their behavioral correlates remain unresolved .
abstract_sentence: Motor cortical beta oscillations have been observed for decades, but their specific behavioral correlates remain unclear.

fact: Three macaque monkeys were trained to volitionally modulate their motor cortical beta oscillations using a novel neurofeedback task before reaching.
source_span: To investigate how changes in population neural activity , beta oscillations , and behavior are linked , we recorded multi-scale neural activity from motor cortex while three macaques performed a novel neurofeedback task . Subjects volitionally brought their beta oscillatory power to an instructed state and subsequently executed an arm reach . To explore how beta oscillations reflect changes in spiking activity and movement parameters , we trained three macaque monkeys to perform a typical center-out arm-reaching task ( CO task , Figure 1a ) , and a novel sequential beta neurofeedback arm-reaching task ( NR task , Figure 1b ). Three male rhesus macaques ( Macaca mulatta ) were chronically implanted with arrays of 128 Teflon-coated tungsten microwire electrodes ... in the left upper arm area of primary motor cortex ( M1 ) and posterior dorsal premotor cortex ( PMd ).
abstract_sentence: The study used a novel neurofeedback task in which three macaque monkeys volitionally modulated their motor cortical beta oscillatory power before performing an arm reach.

fact: Neurofeedback enabled monkeys to increase or decrease motor cortical beta power to target levels before reaching.
source_span: This study uses neurofeedback to manipulate beta oscillations in subjects' motor cortices with the aim of studying effects on arm reaching . Subjects modulated endogenous motor cortical local field potential signals to move the vertical position of the beta cursor ... During NR task performance from these days , subjects exhibited above chance performance ( Figure 1e , see Materials and methods - Chance level performance of beta neurofeedback epoch ). The neurofeedback epoch accomplished the goal of bringing beta power to different levels shown by plotting mean normalized beta power for the last 1 s of the neurofeedback epoch ... At the time of the go cue there is a significant group difference in normalized beta power for the four different neurofeedback target conditions Mean traces show that high and low beta targets were achieved by increasing and decreasing beta power , respectively .
abstract_sentence: Monkeys volitionally modulated their beta oscillatory power to instructed levels before executing arm reaches using neurofeedback.

fact: Lower beta power before reaching is associated with faster movement onset times compared to higher beta power.
source_span: Reaches preceded by a reduction in beta power exhibited significantly faster movement onset times than reaches preceded by an increase in beta power . In all three animals, trials with high beta power targets had subsequent reaches with slower movement onset times (Figure 3a–c, two-tailed Cuzick’s test, Monkey S: z = 5.763, p=8.267e-09, n = 1183, Monkey C: z = 11.987, p<5e-20, n = 2168, Monkey G: z = 5.856, p=4.729e-09, n = 1028). Specifically , as increased beta oscillations during the NR task are correlated with slower MOT times , beta oscillations may reflect a shift in neural population patterns in a way that affects movement onset. Despite the different approaches that were taken to increase and decrease beta power across animals there is still a consistent effect of high versus low beta power on movement onset times , increasing confidence that the oscillation is a reliable marker of the observed behavior .
abstract_sentence: Reaches preceded by reduced beta power had significantly faster movement onset times than those preceded by increased beta power.

fact: Neural population activity is more distant from movement initiation during beta oscillations induced by neurofeedback or occurring naturally.
source_span: Further , population neural activity was found to shift farther from a movement onset state during beta oscillations that were neurofeedback-induced or naturally occurring during reaching tasks . Notably , this shift in neural population was also seen in naturally occurring beta oscillations during reaching tasks , suggesting that beta oscillations reflect a common signature of spiking patterns even in different task contexts. In Figure 7b , traces are aligned to the go cue , showing that during the neurofeedback epoch prior to the go cue , the high beta target ( red ) maintains a much greater distance from the MO threshold than the low and mid-low beta targets ( green and blue ) . At the time of the go cue the high beta target is further from the MO threshold than the lower beta targets , suggesting that subjects must traverse a greater neural distance to arrive at the MO threshold , which may take longer resulting in a longer MOT . During both the center-out (CO) and no-reward (NR) tasks, neural activity chunks with beta oscillations (on-beta) are generally farther from the movement onset threshold than chunks without beta oscillations (off-beta).
abstract_sentence: Population neural activity shifts farther from a movement onset state during beta oscillations, whether neurofeedback-induced or naturally occurring.

fact: Beta oscillations in motor cortex are linked to neural patterns that slow the onset of new movements.
source_span: This finding establishes a population neural basis for slowed movement onset following periods of beta oscillatory activity . Our result that volitionally increasing and decreasing motor cortical beta power with neurofeedback precedes slower and faster movement onset times supports the hypothesis that beta oscillations are linked to neural patterns that slow onset of new movements ( Gilbertson et al . , 2005 ). The hypothesis that encoding of specific movements is compromised with beta oscillations is further supported by experiments showing that ... movement cues associated with more uncertainty are correlated with higher beta power during preparatory periods ... during spike-driven cursor brain-machine interface tasks ... periods of beta oscillatory activity correspond to inferior neural decoding ... and slower cursor movements ... suggesting that the population contains less specific directional information ...
abstract_sentence: The study establishes a population neural basis for slowed movement onset following periods of beta oscillatory activity.

fact: Marburg virus, Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV), and Dengue virus activate and benefit from expression of the transcription regulator nuclear erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2), whereas Nrf2 mobilization counters HIV infection in macrophages.
source_span: Marburg virus , the Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus ( KSHV ) and Dengue virus all activate , and benefit from , expression of the transcription regulator nuclear erythroid 2-related factor 2 ( Nrf2 ) . Finally , the discovery that Nrf2 mobilization counters HIV infection in macrophages stands in contrast with recent work showing that Marburg and Dengue virus as well as KSHV initiate and benefit from increased Nrf2 expression [30 , 32 , 34 , 41] .
abstract_sentence: Some viruses activate and benefit from Nrf2 expression, but HIV infection is affected differently.

fact: The impact of Nrf2 activation on human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection had not been tested prior to this study.
source_span: The impact of Nrf2 activation on human immunodeficiency virus ( HIV ) infection has not been tested .
abstract_sentence: The effect of Nrf2 activation on HIV infection had not been previously studied.

fact: Sulforaphane (SFN), a compound produced in cruciferous vegetables after mechanical damage, mobilizes Nrf2 to potently reprogram cellular gene expression.
source_span: Sulforaphane ( SFN ) , produced in cruciferous vegetables after mechanical damage , mobilizes Nrf2 to potently reprogram cellular gene expression . SFN is a powerful mobilizer of the transcription factor nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 ( Nrf2 ) [22–24] . Nrf2 , a master regulator of the antioxidant response [25 , 26] , ... SFN acts through Nrf2 to execute the majority of its known functions [44–46] .
abstract_sentence: Sulforaphane (SFN) activates Nrf2 by mobilizing it to reprogram cellular gene expression.

fact: SFN blocks HIV infection in primary macrophages but not in primary T cells, showing cell-type specificity of the antiviral effect.
source_span: Here we show for the first time that SFN blocks HIV infection in primary macrophages but not in primary T cells . SFN does not block infection in all cell-types and blocks replication after late reverse transcription products have been formed , all support a model in which the restriction is well after entry into the cell but likely before the viral pre-integration complex is imported into the cell nucleus . The lack of anti-viral SFN action in numerous cell types and the dependence in macrophages solely on Nrf2 ... Further investigation will be required to determine why SFN fails to block infection in T cells , whether the same pathway could be exploited there as well or whether the restriction can be activated directly by other means . Thus, SFN acts to block single-round HIV-1 infections in primary hMDMs but not in primary T cells.
abstract_sentence: SFN blocks HIV infection in primary macrophages but not in primary T cells.

fact: siRNA-mediated depletion of Nrf2 boosts HIV infectivity in primary macrophages and reduces the antiviral effects of SFN treatment, supporting that Nrf2 mediates the antiviral activity.
source_span: Similarly SFN blocks infection in PMA-differentiated promonocytic cell lines , but not in other cell lines tested . siRNA-mediated depletion of Nrf2 boosted HIV infectivity in primary macrophages and reduced the anti-viral effects of SFN treatment . Importantly however , Nrf2 levels remained inversely proportional to infection levels even in the absence of SFN . This supports a model in which HIV infection is countered specifically through Nrf2 , and SFN acts to block HIV by increasing Nrf2 levels . The SFN-regulated restriction relies on Nrf2 , a transcription regulator of anti-oxidant genes . Importantly , we found that macrophages express sufficient Nrf2 to maintain a partial restriction even in the absence of SFN .
abstract_sentence: Nrf2 is required for SFN's antiviral effect in macrophages; depleting Nrf2 increases HIV infectivity and reduces SFN's antiviral effect.

fact: Data are consistent with an Nrf2-dependent block to HIV infection in primary human macrophages that is enhanced by SFN treatment.
source_span: Overall these data are consistent with an Nrf2-dependent block to HIV infection in hMDMs that is enhanced , here , by SFN treatment . Overall these data are consistent with an Nrf2-dependent block to HIV infection in hMDMs that is enhanced , here , by SFN treatment . SFN blocks single-round HIV-1 and HIV-2 infections ( Fig 4 ) . DMF and MMF , like SFN , increase levels of Nrf2 [55] , suggesting that these compounds also block HIV in macrophages through Nrf2 .
abstract_sentence: SFN enhances an Nrf2-dependent block to HIV infection in primary human macrophages.

fact: SFN treatment blocks HIV infection after entry but before formation of 2-LTR circles, indicating a post-entry block similar to SAMHD1 and MX2, but without upregulating these proteins.
source_span: We further found that , like the type I interferon-induced cellular anti-viral proteins SAMHD1 and MX2 , SFN treatment blocks infection after entry , but before formation of 2-LTR circles . This limits the Nrf2-mediated block to steps that extend from attachment of the virus to the cell through transcription from the provirus . ... The vehicle- and SFN-treated samples showed similar levels of late reverse transcription product , indicating that SFN , unlike AZT , did not hinder replication steps from viral entry through reverse transcription ( Fig 7A ) . When we tested for 2-LTR circles ... we found that these were clearly decreased in the AZT and SFN samples relative to the vehicle controls ( Fig 7B ) . Alu-PCR , testing for integrated proviral sequences , also showed that these were similarly decreased in AZT- and SFN-treated cultures ... We found that SFN counters infection whether viral entry is mediated through HIV Env or VSV-G glycoproteins ( Figs 1B versus 5E ) . This suggests a post-entry block as these glycoproteins engage different entry mechanisms .
abstract_sentence: SFN blocks HIV infection after viral entry but before formation of 2-LTR circles, similar to antiviral proteins SAMHD1 and MX2.

fact: Neither SAMHD1 nor MX2 were upregulated by SFN treatment, indicating a distinct antiviral mechanism from interferon-induced pathways.
source_span: Interestingly however , neither SAMHD1 nor MX2 were upregulated . SFN did not significantly change levels of either SAMHD1 or MX2 . Conversely , IFNα treatment increased levels of MX2 as expected . None of the genes known to be modulated by Nrf2 direct production of recognized anti-viral products [28] . It is however possible that Nrf2 initiates a different expression pattern in macrophages than it does in previously tested B lymphocyte-derived cell lines [28] .
abstract_sentence: SFN does not upregulate the antiviral proteins SAMHD1 or MX2 during HIV infection blockade.

fact: Nrf2 action can potently block HIV infection and highlights a novel way to trigger this inhibition, representing a new antiviral state that HIV may not have encountered.
source_span: This shows for the first time that Nrf2 action can potently block HIV infection and highlights a novel way to trigger this inhibition . We thus have discovered in SFN , a new way to activate an anti-viral state that HIV may not have previously encountered . It is therefore unlikely that the virus has developed an effective countermeasure .
abstract_sentence: Nrf2 activation can potently block HIV infection, revealing a novel antiviral mechanism.

abstract_sentence: Aedes-borne arboviruses continue to cause epidemics worldwide.
